result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_directed()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is directed. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3865-L3925){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_directed() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns whether this graph treats edges as directed (with distinct source and target) or undirected (bidirectional connections). This property is set when the graph is created and cannot be changed afterward. In directed graphs: - edge `A->B` is different from `B->A` - each direction must be explicitly added - useful for modeling asymmetric relationships (follows, citations, etc.) In undirected graphs: - edge `A--B` is the same as `B--A` - adding `A--B` automatically adds `B--A` - useful for modeling symmetric relationships (friendship, proximity, etc.) ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is directed, `False` if undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Check graph directionality: ::: {#950602a0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec directed_graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) # Returns True directed_graph.is_directed() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#956e9408 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} undirected_graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) # Returns False undirected_graph.is_directed() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Use directionality to customize behavior: ::: {#c4e86bd8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_node(label="A").add_node(label="B") if graph.is_directed(): # Add both directions for bidirectional relationship graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B") graph.add_edge(source="B", target="A") else: # Single edge suffices for undirected graph.add_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` :::
